title: Community Impact Grants: Fall Cycle
summary: Unrestricted general operating support for nonprofits working in education and youth, arts and culture, environment and land stewardship, and animal welfare in northern Arizona.
description: The Fall Cycle of the Community Impact Grants program provides one-year, unrestricted general operating support to organizations that strengthen learning, creativity, and the natural environment across Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, and Apache counties.
Award amounts are based on the applicant's annual operating budget. The Foundation awarded $612,500 to 46 organizations in the Fall 2026 cycle and expects a similar level of funding in 2027.
impact_areas: Early literacy, math, and school readiness
College and career pathways and opportunity youth re-engagement
Arts access for youth and families and preservation of cultural heritage
Watershed protection, forest restoration, and environmental justice
Local food systems and renewable energy
Spay and neuter access, humane education, and wildlife rehabilitation
populations_served: Families in rural and tribal communities

geography.summary: Organizations must be located in or provide services to residents of Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, or Apache counties, Arizona.

eligibility: Tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3), a public or governmental agency (including public schools), a federally recognized tribe or tribal program, or a project with a qualified fiscal sponsor
Located in or primarily serving residents of Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, or Apache counties
In operation for at least two years with a board-approved annual budget
Non-discriminatory in hiring, board membership, and delivery of services
Work aligns with at least one Fall Cycle field of interest: Education & Youth, History, Arts & Culture, Environment & Land Stewardship, or Animal Welfare
One Community Impact Grant application per organization per calendar year (Spring or Fall, not both)
not_eligible: Organizations that received a Community Impact Grant in calendar year 2026
Individuals, scholarships, or private school tuition
Capital campaigns, endowments, or debt reduction

funding.summary: $5,000 to $25,000, determined by the organization's annual operating budget

dates.info_session: Applicant information session (virtual): Wednesday, July 14, 2027, 10:00 a.m. MST

how_to_apply.intro: Applications are submitted through the CPCF Grant Portal during the open window. The Fall Cycle uses the same application worksheet as the Spring Cycle.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility
steps.text: Review the 2027 Fall Cycle Guidelines and complete the Grant Eligibility Checklist.

steps.title: Prepare your answers
steps.text: Download the Community Impact Grant Application Worksheet and draft your responses.

steps.title: Create or update your portal account
steps.text: New applicants create an organization profile in the CPCF Grant Portal. Returning applicants confirm that their profile is current.

steps.title: Submit the application
steps.text: Submit the online application, operating budget, and most recent financial statements by 5:00 p.m. MST on August 20, 2027.

steps.title: Site visit and decision
steps.text: Program staff may schedule site visits in September and October. Decisions are announced by November 19, 2027.

review_criteria: Alignment with Fall Cycle fields of interest
Evidence of community need and results
Equity: the organization is led by, or meaningfully involves, the communities it serves

reporting.summary: Grantees submit a brief Community Impact Story Report at the end of the grant period.
items: A short narrative (300–500 words) or photo story describing how the grant strengthened the organization
Number of people served during the grant year
Permission indicating whether CPCF may share the story publicly

faq.a: Yes. Public school districts, charter schools, and Bureau of Indian Education schools may apply. A school's award tier is based on the budget of the program or school site, not the full district budget.

faq.q: Can we apply to both the Fall Cycle and the Plateau Indigenous Communities Fund?
faq.a: Yes. The Plateau Fund has a separate review process, and applying to it does not affect Community Impact eligibility.
